newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Specialty shares slump on weak results.
newsitem.headline: Specialty shares slump on weak results.

text.p: Specialty Stores fell on Thursday weighed by a poor set of interim results and fears it could be overstocked in one of its stores, dealers said.
Dealers said there was a perception that one of Specialty's stores, Mr Price, would have difficulty selling its stock.
"There is a feeling that Mr Price is carrying a lot of stock and people are worried about its tradeability," a dealer said.
Specialty shares fell 50 cents to 470 cents and settled 45 cents or 8.65 percent lower at 475 cents around noon. About 120,000 shares valued at 600,000 rand changed hands.

Dealers said Specialty was the flagship performer in the stores sector and if it posted such a "bad" performance, other big stores like Wooltru, Edgars Stores Ltd and Foschini Ltd might also not perform too well.
"If Specialty, which is usually the flagship performer in the group performs so badly, other stores like Woolworths, Edgars and Foschini are not going to do a great deal well," a dealer said.
Despite Specialty posting on Wednesday earnings per share of 7.8 cents for the six months ended August 31 from 7.2 cents, dealers said the market had expected a lot more from it.

"The market expected a hell of a lot from Specialty... (The share) has found a base at this level. I don't think it will go down further. The market feels that the interest rate cycle will turn and that will be good for Specialty," one dealer said.
